---
title: "RSS Climate Slides"
author: "Climate Change Response Program"
date: today
date-format: short
format:
  pptx:
    slide-level: 2
    reference-doc: "RSS-Climate-Slides-Template.pptx"
params:
  SiteID: "ISRO"  # UPDATE
  LongName: "Isle Royale National Park"  # UPDATE
  # region.name: "Midwest"  # UPDATE
  CF_selected: "WarmWet_HotDry"  # Comment in/out depending on pair you choose
  # CF_selected: "WarmDry_HotWet"  # Comment in/out depending on pair you choose
  Base_Park_Dir: "E:/RCF_2024/RCF_opened"  # UPDATE
  map_csv: "climate-metric-title.csv"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

##### DO THIS FIRST #####
# Go to this website and download the zip file of your park unit of interest:
# https://cf-results.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/index.html
# Extract the zip file
# Save the unzipped folder to your R repository (or wherever you prefer it to be)
#####

# Load library packages
# install.packages(c("dplyr","readr","stringr","tools")) # If you have not installed these packages yet, run this line of code
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(tools)

# Pull parameters from YAML
SiteID        <- params$SiteID
LongName      <- params$LongName
region.name   <- params$region.name
CF_selected   <- params$CF_selected
Base_Park_Dir <- params$Base_Park_Dir
MapCSV        <- params$map_csv

# Park-specific directory
Park_CF_Dir <- file.path(Base_Park_Dir, SiteID)

# ---- Dynamic climate future directories ----
if (CF_selected == "WarmWet_HotDry") {
  CFs   <- c("Warm Wet", "Hot Dry")
  CF_abbreviation <- "WW-HD"
  CFDir <- file.path(Park_CF_Dir, "WarmWet_HotDry")
  col <- c("#2B83BA", "#D7191C")
  color.names <- c("blue", "red")
} else {
  CFs   <- c("Warm Dry", "Hot Wet")
  CF_abbreviation <- "WD-HW"
  CFDir <- file.path(Park_CF_Dir, "WarmDry_HotWet")
  col <- c("#FDAE61", "#ABDDA4")
  color.names <- c("orange", "green")
}

# ---- Figures directory (all images live here) ----
FigDir <- file.path(CFDir, "figures")

# ---- Read mapping CSV ----
mapping <- read_csv(MapCSV, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    file_name  = str_trim(tolower(file_name)),
    title      = str_trim(title),
    subheading = str_trim(subheading)
  )

lookup <- mapping %>% select(file_name, title, subheading)

# ---- Collect image files ----
files <- list.files(
  FigDir,
  pattern = "\\.(png|jpg|jpeg|tif|tiff|gif|bmp|svg)$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)
files <- files[order(tolower(basename(files)))]

# ---- Slide creation helper ----
make_slide <- function(img_path) {

  base <- basename(img_path)
  key  <- tolower(base)

  row <- lookup %>% filter(file_name == key)

  # title from CSV or fallback
  if (nrow(row) == 1 && !is.na(row$title) && row$title != "") {
    slide_title <- row$title
  } else {
    slide_title <- toTitleCase(gsub("[-_]+"," ",
       file_path_sans_ext(base)))
  }

  # subheading from CSV or empty
  if (nrow(row) == 1 && !is.na(row$subheading) && row$subheading != "") {
    subhead <- row$subheading
  } else {
    subhead <- ""
  }

  # fix path for Windows
  p2 <- gsub("\\\\", "/", normalizePath(img_path, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE))

  # emit slide
  cat('## ', slide_title, ' {layout="Title and Content"}', "\n\n", sep = "")
  if (subhead != "") {
    cat(subhead, "\n\n")
  }
  cat("![](", p2, "){width=10in height=7.5in}\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r generate-slides, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
for (img in files) {
  make_slide(img)
}
```
